translation.text: Look, another house was greater than that one. All its doorways stood open before me, and it was built with tongues of fire.[a]

footnotes.text: The larger-house comparison and the open-door statement are both retained. Actual Dillmann cols111 and606 control the building and door expressions. “Tongues of fire” preserves the selected image rather than making an architectural reconstruction.

translation.text: In every respect it excelled in splendor, honor, and greatness, so that its splendor and greatness cannot be described to you.[a]

footnotes.text: The selected negative ability-and-telling construction does not mention anyone’s eyes. This English retains inability to describe, checked in actual cols1063–1064 and1381, rather than importing the older unsupported alternate about eyes being unable to look.

translation.text: Its floor was fire; above it were lightning and the courses of the stars, and its ceiling was blazing fire.[a]

footnotes.text: The selected floor, above, star-course and ceiling clauses are distinct and all retained. Actual Dillmann cols217,309,683 and1249–1250 support the architectural and fiery imagery. These are features of the narrated vision, not a verified physical construction.

translation.text: I looked and saw within it a lofty throne. Its appearance was like crystal, its circle like the shining sun, and the voice of the cherubim.[a]

footnotes.text: Actual Dillmann col331 supports crystal/ice for the appearance noun and col848 supports circle/orbit. The selected text ends with “and the voice of the cherubim,” without a complete relation to the preceding features. I do not certify an added hearing verb or silently choose wheels for the circle word. This whole proposed unit is held until that central relation is addressed.
